supersedes_reason: C8's provenance claim was FALSE and nothing could see it. C8 declared head_commit 4022385, where .codex/hooks/subagent_stop_validate.py hashes to 0533da88 -- the very value C8 itself said had gone stale -- while the bytes it attested first exist at 9df6cd4, C8's own sealing commit. A round-13 registered adjudicator found it (F-R13-05); check_canary_freshness.py could not, because it compared attested digests against the WORKING TREE and never against the declared commit. C8 is NOT edited: a retained attestation is evidence and is retired by replacement.
the_structural_cause: This was not carelessness, it was an impossible field. A canary is dispatched as the last act BEFORE the sealing commit, so at the moment it writes its attestation the commit that will contain its bytes does not exist. `git rev-parse HEAD` therefore returns the PREVIOUS commit, which is structurally the wrong answer, and every canary in this chain that changed a hook would have recorded the same lie. C8 is simply the one where it mattered, because C8 is the canary that ran when the hooks HAD changed.
the_fix: head_commit is written as PENDING_COMMIT and pinned by a follow-up commit -- exactly the convention SSOT_FACTS.json already uses for a declared fact's as_of_commit. check_canary_freshness.py now verifies it: a concrete hash must contain the attested bytes, and PENDING_COMMIT is legal only in the commit that introduces the attestation, because requiring the pin in that same commit would be unsatisfiable.
method: Identical to C8: Start dispatched with ACTIVE_RUN naming the canary run so a real lease exists, ACTIVE_RUN repointed to the DECOY, then ONE shell command copies the pointer to a raw file, writes date -u to nanoseconds, dispatches SubagentStop, records its exit status, writes the closing clock, copies the pointer again, and copies ADMISSIONS.jsonl on both sides.
what_this_does_not_claim: Nothing about the shared-OS-user residual. It moves no gate. It also does NOT re-close the second C8 defect (F-R13-04): C8's ledger-pinned envelope cited the un-suffixed attempt-1 files, whose bracket contains no consume. C11 avoids that by construction -- it had no blocked first attempt and its envelope cites the artifact and the ledger rather than a specific attempt's raw files -- but the general guard, that cited evidence must SUPPORT the claim, is not yet written.
